Test Case Name: USA Website Timezone is Set to a Valid US Timezone
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Locale Options > Timezone
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > General > Locale Options
5. Read the Timezone dropdown value
Expected Result: Timezone value contains 'America/' prefix (e.g. America/Chicago, America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles). Must NOT contain 'Australia'.
Why It Matters: Incorrect timezone produces wrong order timestamps, scheduled email times, and order processing windows for US customers.

Test Case Name: Locale Language & Format is Set to United States English (en_US)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Locale Options > Locale
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > General > Locale Options
5. Read the Locale dropdown value
Expected Result: Locale = en_US (English - United States). Label must contain 'United States'. Must NOT be en_AU.
Why It Matters: AU locale (en_AU) formats dates (DD/MM/YYYY), numbers, and currency differently to US standards (MM/DD/YYYY). This governs all date and number formatting across the US storefront.

Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Store Information > Country

Test Case Name: Store Address City is Set to a US City (Not an Australian City)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Store Information > City
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > General > Store Information
5. Read the City input field value
Expected Result: City is non-empty. Must NOT contain: Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Canberra, Darwin, Hobart.

Test Case Name: Store Address State is a Valid US State (Not an Australian State)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Store Information > Region / State
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > General > Store Information
5. Read the Region/State dropdown or input value
Expected Result: State is non-empty. Must NOT be: VIC, NSW, QLD, SA, WA, TAS, NT, ACT, or their full names.
Why It Matters: State drives US tax rate computation (Avalara) and US carrier rate lookups (UPS, FedEx). An AU state value will cause tax and shipping calculation failures.

Test Case Name: Store ZIP Code is a Valid 5-Digit US ZIP (Not a 4-Digit AU Postcode)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > General > Store Information > ZIP / Postal Code
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > General > Store Information
5. Read the Postcode input field value
Expected Result: ZIP code is non-empty and matches regex: ^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$ (e.g. 60601 or 60601-1234). Must NOT be a 4-digit AU postcode (e.g. 3000).
Why It Matters: Used on invoices and US carrier shipping rate lookups (UPS, FedEx). A 4-digit AU postcode will fail US carrier ZIP validation and break shipping rate calculation.

Test Steps:

3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > General > State Options
5. Inspect the 'State is Required for' multi-select list

Test Case Name: Public HTTP Base URL is Bound to the US Domain (globewest.com, Not .com.au)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > Web > Base URLs > Base URL
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > Web > Base URLs
5. Read the Base URL input field value
Expected Result: Base URL contains 'globewest.com' (US domain). Must NOT contain '.com.au'. Must NOT be empty.

Test Case Name: Secure HTTPS Base URL is Bound to the US Domain with Valid HTTPS Protocol
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > Web > Base URLs (Secure) > Secure Base URL
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel

Test Case Name: Product Image & Media Base URL Points to US Location (Not AU Domain)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > Web > Base URLs > Base URL for User Media Files
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > Web > Base URLs
5. Read the Base URL for User Media Files input value
Expected Result: If populated: must NOT contain '.com.au'. If fully qualified (starts with http), must contain 'globewest.com'. Empty/relative value is acceptable (inherits base URL).
Why It Matters: Incorrect media URL serves product images from the AU domain, causing broken product images, CORS errors, and CDN misconfiguration on the US B2B storefront.

Test Case Name: Base Currency and Default Display Currency are Both Configured as USD (Not AUD)
Admin Navigation Path: Stores > Configuration > [US Scope] > General > Currency Setup > Currency Options
Test Steps:
1. Login to Magento Admin Panel
2. Go to Stores > Configuration
3. Switch scope to GlobeWest US store-view
4. Navigate to General > Currency Setup > Currency Options
5. Read Base Currency dropdown value

Expected Result: Base Currency contains 'USD'. Default Display Currency contains 'USD'. Neither must contain 'AUD'.

Test Case Name: US Storefront Prices Display in USD — AUD and GST Labels Not Shown to US Customers
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to US Homepage: https://mcstaging2.globewest.com
2. Verify URL is on globewest.com (not .com.au)
3. Navigate to PLP: /indoor
4. Check price element displays '$' symbol (not 'AUD')
5. Navigate to PDP product URL
6. Check price element displays '$' symbol
7. Verify no GST notice/label is visible on the PDP
Expected Result: All prices show '$' (USD format). 'AUD', 'A$', and 'GST' are NOT visible anywhere to US customers.
Why It Matters: End-to-end verification that all admin currency config flows through correctly to the customer-facing US B2B storefront. GST is AU-specific — US customers must never see it.
